sentences.text: Revenue compounded from $1.70 billion in FY2016 [F1] to $12.0 billion in FY2025 [F10], a 24.2% CAGR [F196].
Growth came in steps: revenue rose 49.1% in FY2020 [D194] but only 8.9% in FY2025 [D446].
The FY2020 jump followed TRIKAFTA's U.S. approval and KAFTRIO's EU approval, which the filing names as the main driver [D194][P53].
Operating margin fell 40.9pp to -2.1% in FY2024 [D408][F34], which the filing ties to $4.4 billion of Alpine-related acquired R&D [P11].
In FY2025 revenue grew 8.9% [D446]; ALYFTREK, in its first year at $838 million [S69], added 7.6pp [D590].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO added only 0.7pp [D531], and the FY2025 filing excerpt cuts off before stating a cause [P3].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO still made up 85.9% of revenue in FY2025 [D529], down from 92.9% in FY2024 [D526].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO added 26.3pp in FY2022 [D522], which the filing ties to international launches and continued U.S. performance [P31].
Over FY2022 to FY2025 revenue compounded at 10.4% [D679], while operating income's CAGR was -1.0% [D681].
Operating margin of 34.8% [F35] is 3.0pp above its window median of 31.8% [D663] and 13.4pp below the FY2022 high of 48.2% [D662].
In FY2024 the residual line took 37.2pp of the 40.9pp fall [D424][D408], far more than cost of revenue, R&D or SG&A [D421][D422][D423].
The acquired R&D the filing describes for FY2024 [P11] is the likely content of that residual [D424].
The FY2025 recovery of 36.9pp [D452] was mostly that residual, +37.7pp [D468], while cost of revenue, R&D and SG&A moved +0.1pp, +0.4pp and -1.3pp [D465][D466][D467].
Cost of revenue was 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 [D425], which the filing links to a lower overall CF royalty rate [P4].
The filing attributes operating cash flow of $3.63 billion [F85] mainly to operating income of $4.17 billion [F25][P1].
Operating cash flow was 0.92x net income [D434] and free cash flow 0.81x [D435], against a 1.07x window median [D675].
Receivables grew 27.6% [D461] and inventory 39.9% [D462] in FY2025, and the excerpts provided do not explain that build.
Capex rose 47.0% to $438 million [D447][F95], 2.09x D&A [D436], and no passage in the pack explains the step-up.
Net cash was $12.3 billion at FY2025 year-end [D439], 102.7% of revenue [D440], against a peer median of -50.7% [D692] and an 88th percentile rank [D691].
Cash and investments fell 18.2% in FY2024 [D416], which the filing attributes mainly to the Alpine payment and buybacks [P10].
The current ratio was 2.90x in FY2025 [F185], below its 3.52x window median [D678] though above the 2.31x low [D676].
Buybacks and dividends of $2.02 billion [D441] were 63.2% of free cash flow [D442], while diluted shares stayed flat at 258.0m [X137][D459].
Inventory days rose from 287 to 373 [D397][D444], and inventory of $1.69 billion [X178] exceeded FY2025 cost of revenue of $1.65 billion [X30].
Inventory days were 135 in FY2016 [D19], so the rise is multi-year, and the excerpts provided do not explain it.
Acquired R&D is lumpy: $4.6 billion in FY2024 [P11] against $1.11 billion in FY2021 [X46], and the company expects it to keep fluctuating [P29].
The FY2025 tax-rate swing [R2] is benign: the FY2024 315.5% rate [D390] reflected non-deductible Alpine acquired R&D [P5].
Inventory days above 373 [D444] in the FY2026 10-K would confirm the build is persisting; a fall toward 287 [D397] would show it reversing.
SG&A above 14.6% of revenue [D427] in the FY2026 10-K would mean launch spending is still outrunning sales; below 13.3% [D384] would show leverage returning.
Free cash flow to net income back above the 1.07x window median [D675] in the FY2026 10-K would show working capital no longer absorbing cash; FY2025 was 0.81x [D435].
